title: which of the latest spellings opened outside the 36 twin families resolve to a file that exists?

evidence_definition.the_literal_names_a_path_that_exists_on_: the literal carries a directory and that path exists under the repo root
evidence_definition.the_literal_names_a_path_that_does_not_e: the literal carries a directory that does not exist, but a file with that basename is on disk somewhere (existence proved, address not proved)
evidence_definition.a_bare_basename_and_exactly_one_file_in_: the literal is a bare basename and exactly one file in the tree has it
evidence_definition.a_bare_basename_and_several_files_in_the: the literal is a bare basename and several files have it: existence is proved, the directory is not (E366's two address forms)
evidence_definition.the_spelling_carries_no_concrete_name_so: the spelling has no concrete name ('%s_latest.json', '_latest.json'), so no single file can be the thing it names
evidence_definition.no_file_in_the_tree_carries_this_spellin: nothing in the tree carries this spelling

class_definition.a_file_carries_this_spelling_and_a_sourc: some site resolves to a file and a source writes that spelling
class_definition.a_file_carries_this_spelling_but_no_sour: some site resolves to a file that no source in the corpus writes
class_definition.no_file_carries_this_spelling_although_a: no site resolves but a source writes the spelling: the reader and the writer disagree about the path, or the writer has not run yet
class_definition.no_file_carries_this_spelling_and_no_sou: no site resolves and no source writes it: a reader of a face nothing produces
class_definition.the_spelling_names_no_concrete_file_at_a: every site for this spelling is a template that carries no name

method_limits: the population is E479's rule: an opener literal whose basename ends in '_latest.json' and belongs to none of the 36 twins. A plain 'latest.json' does not end with the suffix and is not in this population (its own census is E417's)
existence is judged against the tree as it stands at run time; a writer that has not run yet produces a dead_read_writer row, and the class says which of the two it is
a bare basename is proved to exist but never proved to be the file the reader means (E366); the row publishes how many files carry it
the scan reads .py sources that mention the suffix and follows e470's one-hop name resolution, so a path composed through an argument or an environment variable is invisible
this census excludes its own runner and the E479/E480/E481/E484 families so it cannot count its own literals (E180/E207 family)
the parent published 689 opener sites where this face counts distinct (source, line, literal) triples: the two site tallies are different measurements, and only the source tally (147) is compared
resolving a spelling to a file is not the same as reading its content; E477/E478/E481 own what the bytes cost and whether two vintages agree
